 Live .  67,651 viewing 67651 viewing Live page Updated 2 minutes ago Flights grounded across US as homeland security secretary says no indication of an attack
 FAA Orders Rare Grounding of All US Flights
 BBC News
 Close Watch live Summary
 Flights have been grounded across the US due to an air traffic control communications issue
 There's no indication that this is an attack against the US, the homeland security secretary says, adding that "everybody's safe"
 US aviation officials earlier issued an order to ground all flights due to "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety"
 Several major airports confirmed the ground stop 
 There's currently no indication of when the order will be lifted
 Close form Have you been affected?
 Get in touch Live Reporting
 Edited by Dulcie Lee in Washington DC
 US seeks to reassure public - but there are more questions than answers published at 22:22 GMT 22:22 GMT 
 Daniel Bush 
Washington correspondent 
 Image source, Reuters US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has just sought to reassure the public that the nationwide air traffic outage wasn't caused by a "nefarious act".
 He said repeatedly that this "isn’t another 9/11".
 But beyond that, he made clear there are more questions than answers about what's going on.
 The administration is working to address what he said was a "telecommunications outage". But he acknowledged the government doesn't know what caused it or how long it'll take to fix.
 Mullin also said that he couldn’t "rule anything out" as a reason for the outage, despite saying that there was no current indication of an attack.
 It's worth noting that up until now Mullin has been best known for overseeing a ramp-up of the administration’s immigration deportation program. This crisis will test his leadership atop the agency in charge of protecting the US homeland.

 'There's some confusion' - BBC presenter stuck at Denver Airport published at 22:15 GMT 22:15 GMT 
 The BBC's Chief Presenter Sumi Somaskanda recently arrived at Denver Airport and says "there's some confusion" there.
 She says the screens at the airport announcing when flights are leaving haven't caught up following news of the ground stop. 
 "You have a number of people here who are checking in bags, who are going to the counters to try and get ready for their flights and head over to security but they're now hearing there's a groundstop."
 Among those also at the airport is US Congressman Ro Khanna, who, like the BBC, was at a Democratic conference earlier on Friday. 
 Somaskanda says that while people have started to gather, "it's going to become very chaotic as more and more people realise that none of these flights are going anywhere".

 Public should not be fearful - Mullin published at 22:12 GMT 22:12 GMT 
 We've just heard from Markwayne Mullin, who leads the US Department of Homeland Security. He says:
 A "telecommunications outage" has led to the ground stop 
 The Federal Aviation Administration has grounded all flights "out of an abundance of caution"
 He tells journalists gathered at the White House that everybody is safe, all flights are accounted for and "there should be no fear to the public at all"
 "This isn't another 9/11," he says. "This is a telecommunication outage, this is much different"
 He adds that there is no reason to connect today's issues to the ongoing Microsoft outage
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Issue not connected to Microsoft outage - Mullin published at 22:08 GMT 22:08 GMT 
 Mullin says the focus at the moment is on restoring communication and to "get all the flights down" on the ground.
 He adds there isn't "any reason" to connect today's issues with Microsoft and the current outage.
 "We have not discussed any time frame," he says when asked about the potential length of the issues.
 "It's going to take some time."

 'Everybody's safe' - Mullin published at 22:05 GMT 22:05 GMT 
 Image source, Reuters "Everybody's safe," the homeland security secretary adds, saying this isn't "another 9/11".
 He recalls that the last time a national groundstop was issued was during the 9/11 attacks in 2001, before adding this isn't "another 9/11".
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 No indication of an attack - homeland security secretary published at 22:03 GMT 22:03 GMT Breaking 
 US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin is speaking to reporters at the White House now.
 He says there is no indication this was an attack against the United States. 
 "This is a telecommunications outage," he says.
 "All the flights are accounted for," he says.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Several airports confirm ground stop published at 21:45 GMT 21:45 GMT Breaking 
 Several airports have confirmed flights have been grounded after the FAA's announcement, with many advising passengers to check their flight status directly with their airline.
 Those issuing statements include:
 Atlanta Airport , external 
 Washington DC's Reagan Airport , external 
 Miami International Airport , external 
 BWI Marshall Airport , external 
 George Bush Intercontinental Airport , external 
 The FAA adds that a ground stop and delays are possible at:
 LA International Airport (LAX)
 Harry Reid International in Las Vegas
 JFK
 Philadelphia International
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Passenger tells of people stuck on plane in Los Angeles published at 21:41 GMT 21:41 GMT 
 A passenger stuck on a plane at Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) says flights which have just landed are not being allowed to move from the tarmac to the gates.
 The passenger, who has travelled from Newark, tells the BBC's US partner CBS News that they're unable to taxi to the gate as another plane scheduled to take off is not being allowed to depart.
 Another passenger who just landed in Austin tells the broadcaster he and fellow travellers have been told they should "sit tight" as they're also unable to leave the plane.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 More than 3,000 flights currently bound for US airports - Flightradar24 published at 21:34 GMT 21:34 GMT Breaking 
 Image source, Flightradar24 Flight-tracking website Flightradar24 says 3,100 airborne aircraft are currently bound for US airports. 
 On X, it says that no additional aircraft are taking off at this time.
 In its statement, the FAA said inbound international flights would be managed on a "case by case basis".
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Transport secretary says 'communication issue' has hit traffic control centres published at 21:23 GMT 21:23 GMT Breaking 
 Transport Secretary Sean Duffy says the FAA "issued a nationwide ground stop for all US airports following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.
 "FAA technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide immediate updates as we have them," he says.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 US aviation officials order nationwide ground stop published at 21:21 GMT 21:21 GMT Breaking 
 The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says all flights in the US are grounded "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety".
 The alert, which appeared on the FAA website, has since been removed - it's unclear how many flights are currently grounded.
 This is a breaking news story. We’ll bring you more on this shortly.
